#### 1. tooth agenesis, selective, 4  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT10A (HGNC:13829) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP471); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP471) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial morphology (HP:0000276); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP471) —LEADS_TO→ Hypodontia (HP:0000777). Loss-of-function mutations in WNT10A disrupt the Wnt signaling pathway, which is crucial for both craniofacial development and tooth morphogenesis, leading to abnormal facial morphology (Schöpf-Schulz-Passarge syndrome) and hypodontia (tooth agenesis, selective, 4).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in WNT10A with a documented gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in patients with either Schöpf-Schulz-Passarge syndrome or tooth agenesis, selective, 4, or the absence of any WNT10A variants in well-characterized cohorts of these diseases. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common (>1%) pathogenic variant in WNT10A that is not associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT10A in these syndromes could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting the Wnt signaling pathway for the treatment of both craniofacial and dental developmental anomalies.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in WNT10A in individuals with Schöpf-Schulz-Passarge syndrome or odonto-onycho-dermal dysplasia that do not segregate with the phenotype, or evidence of a distinct causal gene for either disease. _(variant: None)_

#### 3. mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.400)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT10A (HGNC:13047) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP501); WNT4 (HGNC:12725) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP501); WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP501) —LEADS_TO→ Branchial arch defects (HP:0001383); WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP501) —LEADS_TO→ Mullerian duct aplasia (HP:0000018); WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP501) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperandrogenism (HP:0004893). Loss-of-function mutations in WNT10A cause Schöpf-Schulz-Passarge syndrome, leading to disruptions in the WNT signaling pathway and resulting in branchial arch defects. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in WNT4 cause mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism, also through disruption of the WNT signaling pathway, affecting Mullerian duct development and androgen regulation.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in WNT10A who do not exhibit features of Schöpf-Schulz-Passarge syndrome, or individuals with pathogenic variants in WNT4 who do not exhibit features of mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism, would challenge this hypothesis. Furthermore, demonstrating that the WNT signaling pathway disruption in each disease has distinct downstream effectors that do not overlap would also falsify this link. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in WNT10A or WNT4 in gnomAD that are associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT signaling in these distinct developmental processes could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting WNT pathway modulation for developmental abnormalities affecting craniofacial and reproductive systems.
